cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Talk Around the Mess
cards.instruction: Keep attention on minor details so no one addresses the larger responsibility you avoided.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Mum's coming for lunch. Is this spoon clean enough for her?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The spoon's fine. You haven't cleaned the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. She checks cutlery. Could you check the forks while I finish this?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've told her to bring rubber gloves and help you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we need a guest towel. Can you help me choose one without a faded stripe?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 claim authority, but A5 ordinary towel-choice request does not sustain approval as the distraction tactic.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 unclean kitchen causes A3 fork inspection; B4 incoming gloved help causes A5 guest-towel selection, after an unrelated restriction.

relationship.evidence: B2 identifies the neglected work and B4 recruits actual help, giving A practical solutions to divert.

heightening.evidence: B4 help would force cleaning, so A5 converts its arrival into another small preparation detail.

specificity.evidence: A1 Mum lunch and B2 A unclean kitchen establish the larger duty explicitly.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 faded-stripe concern is earned by B4 gloved visitor, but the A3 stock authority phrase slows the evasion.
